title: Temporal semantics
summary: Publication date, effective date, observation time, and approval time serve different purposes.

sections.label: Proposed representation
sections.text: Keep when a source was published separate from when a rule applies, when your system retrieved it, and when a reviewed assertion became approved. Use source and dataset versions to reproduce past answers.

sections.label: Exact operations
sections.text: Parse and compare dates in deterministic code. Treat missing date components explicitly rather than letting a model guess.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Historical and current queries use the intended applicability window. A later publication or retrieval does not automatically supersede an earlier effective period.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Requirements and evidence, Development, Tests and review. Use when a requirement depends on dates, an implementation compares applicability windows or a review must reproduce current and historical answers. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Produce a field contract that separates publication, effective period, retrieval and approval times, including missing components.
Check output to obtain: Prepare expected before-start, at-start, at-end and after-end outcomes under the explicitly chosen interval convention.
Check output to obtain: Record observed historical and current results with source and dataset revisions. Do not infer supersession from a later retrieval time.

catalog.applicability: Use when a rule, source or assertion carries more than one date and you must keep publication, effective period, retrieval time and approval time apart, or when historical queries must reproduce a past answer from recorded source and dataset versions.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
